meaning: to go to bed to sleep
literal_translation: ir para a cama para dormir
example: I was very tired, so I hit the sack at nine o'clock.
origin: Probably from older times, when beds were simple sacks filled with straw

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hit someone with a bag
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom has nothing to do with violence or bags.
This is the opposite idea, because hitting the sack means going to sleep, not getting up.
This describes working fast, but the idiom is about going to bed for the night.

explanation: 'Hit the sack' is an informal phrase for going to bed. It is common in everyday speech, especially when someone is tired and ready to sleep.
